note: Appended alongside external-loop-runtime-wiring.json rather than replacing it. That file records what was verified offline; this one records what real GitHub Actions runs proved, including one thing the offline work could only infer.

result.Ingest external signals: SKIPPED - correct. The job holds live credentials and calls out to GitHub, PostHog, Stripe and the ledger; it must never run on an untrusted head.

credential_state.claim: None of the external credentials exist in this repository. Proven, not inferred.
credential_state.how: The runner printed its own env block for the Ingest step of run 34172815714. Every value is empty except the token GitHub injects itself.

observed.GITHUB_TOKEN: set (masked) - injected by Actions, not configured by anyone

credential_state.why_it_matters: Until this run, 'the credentials are missing' was an inference from the authoring sandbox, where they would be absent whether or not the repository had them. It is now an observation from the environment that would actually use them. The Stripe lane is not untested because of a code problem; there is nothing to authenticate with.

defect_found_by_this_run.what: A correctly-reported BLOCKED state failed the workflow instead of warning.
defect_found_by_this_run.detail: GitHub runs every step under `bash -e`. The ingest pipeline exits 2 by design when no store is configured, which aborted the step immediately - the `code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` check and its warning branch were never reached. The branch existed and had never once been able to execute.
defect_found_by_this_run.fix: `set +e` around the pipeline only, keeping pipefail so the node exit code is still the one read, then `set -e` restored.
defect_found_by_this_run.verified: Simulated under the exact runner invocation (`bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`): the warning branch is taken and the step exits 0. A confirming run on a real runner is queued behind the market-ingest concurrency group; see rerun below for its state at the time this file was written.
defect_found_by_this_run.note: Pre-existing on main, not introduced here. It only became visible once a run actually reached the BLOCKED path.

rerun.state_at_write_time: QUEUED - held by concurrency group 'market-ingest' (cancel-in-progress: false) behind the pull_request run on the same head. Not yet confirmed on a real runner.
rerun.not_claimed: The fix is proven by simulation under the identical shell invocation, not yet by a completed GitHub-hosted run.

repository_dispatch.result: AUTH BLOCKER. An unauthenticated POST to /repos/stratumpraxis/stratum-praxis/dispatches returns 403, and this environment holds no token with contents:write - GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN are 14-character placeholders.
repository_dispatch.what_is_proven_instead: The dispatch source itself runs: the CLI was executed end to end against a real client_payload file, refused two forged payment claims, and treated a replay as an upsert. What is not proven is the network hop from Make into GitHub.
repository_dispatch.not_claimed: A real repository_dispatch has not been received by this workflow.

state_machine_reached.path: external event -> dispatch -> normalize -> correlate -> existing asset fit -> QUALIFIED -> ACTIONABLE
state_machine_reached.why: HUMAN_SIGNAL and CHECKOUT need a live PostHog read; PAID and WON need a Stripe payment record. Both are credential-blocked, and neither may be simulated - the state machine refuses every substitute by design.
state_machine_reached.exploration: OPEN - no route has produced verified payment evidence, so there is nothing yet to exploit.

next_blocker: Repository secrets. STRIPE_SECRET_KEY answers the standing clicks-versus-payments question; POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY and POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID open the human-signal lane; SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (plus a unique constraint on signal_id) make the ledger durable. A token with contents:write proves the Make -> GitHub hop.
